audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.difficulty and the Final Matchup Rating both call this an 'Even matchup' while full.diff reads HARD and content win[] hands Lillia the first four stages. Three fields, two answers.
audit.why: Kassadin sits at 40% over 15 games here and the level chart concedes levels 1-5; 'Even' tells the player to contest stages the same page says he loses.
audit.corrected: Wording changed to 'Hard matchup' in both places so it agrees with diff=HARD and the chart. diffRating left at 5.5/10 — 15 games is too thin a sample to move the number on.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike was described qualitatively — 'her R sleep', 'her movespeed gap' — with no cooldowns anywhere, and phases[4] promised mobility at 6 without naming what actually decides the level-6 fight.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s at 500 range and Lilting Lullaby is 150/130/110s. Those two numbers are the whole level-6 conversation and neither appeared.
audit.corrected: Riftwalk's 500 range and 5s rank-1 cooldown added to phases[4] and the cooldown block; Lilting Lullaby's 150/130/110s and Swirlseed's flat 12s added alongside them.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction of the matchup is absent from both layers: Lilting Lullaby only drowses enemies who already carry Dream Dust from her passive. The pages treat her ult as an unconditional lockdown you must dodge.
audit.why: Riot's text is explicit — 'Lillia causes all enemies with Dream Dust on them to become Drowsy before falling asleep.' A Kassadin who breaks contact and lets the dust fall off walks into her ult range immune to it, which is exactly the engage he needs at 6.
audit.corrected: Dream Dust is now the tracked resource in tldr, winCon, enemyWin, loading, spikes[1], phases[3], phases[4], dontsFull[1] and Key Ability Interactions — engage clean and the 110s ult grabs nothing.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late claimed Void Stone and the Q shield 'blank some of her burst'. Blooming Blows deals extra TRUE damage on its edge, which neither touches.
audit.why: Riot's Blooming Blows text: 'dealing extra true damage on the edge.' Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic damage and Void Stone reduces magic damage — both are blind to the rim.
audit.corrected: Stated in content.late, whys[2] and dosFull[0].d, with the actionable half attached: stand inside the ring, not on its edge.

audit.whatIsWrong: Lillia's spin was called 'her W spin' in four places. Watch Out! Eep! is the W — a delayed area bomb. The spin is Blooming Blows (Q).
audit.why: Two different abilities on two different cooldowns (Q 6/5.5/5/4.5/4 vs W 14/13/12/11/10); a player timing a step-up off the wrong one steps into the other.
audit.corrected: Both names used correctly in spikes[0], wants.you[0], wants.foe[0], early and whys[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid said to use 'Force Pulse once our casts have shaved its cooldown', while phases[2].why said 'E only charges when spells fly'. The two contradict each other and only one is current.
audit.why: Force Pulse stopped being a charge-gated ability in V12.23; it is now a normal 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown that ability casts within 1800 units shorten by a second each. The charge framing is three years stale, and the kit file still carries the old tooltip wording. Against Lillia it matters concretely — she casts Blooming Blows every 4-6s, so the cone comes back far faster than its printed cooldown.
audit.corrected: Both strings rewritten to the cooldown-reduction model with the real 21s base, in content.mid, phases[2].why and breakdown.mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block had no numbers at all — 'catch her early in the chase or not at all' and 'hold the R for the fight that decides something'.
audit.why: The punishable cooldown in this lane is Swirlseed at a flat 12s (her only disengage) and Lilting Lullaby at up to 150s. Neither was named.
audit.corrected: Both written into breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Void Stone's second clause — Kassadin ignores unit collision — appears nowhere, despite this being a lane he spends hugging his own wave.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Kassadin takes reduced magic damage and ignores unit collision.' Against a poke champion who wants him stuck on minions, walking through his own wave is free repositioning.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.late told the player to 'Q-silence the counterplay'. Null Sphere has no silence.
audit.why: Riot's text is damage, a channel interrupt, and a magic shield. The silence was removed from Kassadin's kit years ago and the sentence tells a player to rely on a button that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the shield, which is the real effect.

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr, tradeGood, dosFull[1] and dontsFull[1] all refer to Lillia as 'him' and 'his', and tradeBad calls her a juggernaut.
audit.why: Generic filler text left in place; it also mis-sells the lane, since Lillia beats Kassadin by kiting, not by winning a straight exchange.
audit.corrected: Rewritten in the second person against the correct champion and the correct threat.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late stated Void Stone as '15% magic reduction'. It has been 10% since V11.24.
audit.why: A stale number that overstates Kassadin's defensive layer by half. It appears across nearly every Kassadin matchup page, not just this one.
audit.corrected: Set to 10% in content.late. Same character count, so it applies cleanly anywhere else it appears.

edits.before: I concede this lane hard pre-6 and I have to accept it. Lillia's E Swirlseed pokes me from outside my Null Sphere range and her W spin chips me whenever I step up, and her passive DOT keeps burning after she has already danced away on the bonus movespeed — my Q shield can soak one hit but my mana is too thin to keep trading. Do not chase a Q onto her; she just strides off with E/W speed and I eat more DOT for nothing. Hug the wave, last-hit with the tip of Q, and survive to 6.
edits.after: I concede this lane hard pre-6 and I have to accept it. Swirlseed reaches 700 and my Null Sphere only 650, so she pokes from outside my range, and Blooming Blows spins every 4-6s whenever I step up while Dream Dust keeps burning after she has danced away. My Q shield soaks magic, but the rim of Blooming Blows is true damage and my mana is too thin to keep trading anyway. Do not chase a Q onto her. Hug the wave, last-hit with the tip of Q, and survive to 6.

edits.before: Level 6 is my only real window. Riftwalk finally gives me the blink to close her movespeed gap, and the single most important thing here is sidestepping her R — if she lands the drowsy and the sleep procs on my engage I am locked out and dead. Bait the R or wait for it on cooldown, then Riftwalk in, Nether Blade auto for the mana and burst, and Force Pulse once our casts have shaved its cooldown. Even so, one good window does not flip the lane; I am buying time, not taking over.
edits.after: Level 6 is my only real window. Riftwalk gives me a 500-unit blink to close her gap, and the single most important thing here is Dream Dust: Lilting Lullaby only drowses enemies already carrying it, so if I arrive clean her 110-second ult has nothing to grab. Force Pulse is a 21-second cone and every cast near me shaves a second off it, so her spam keeps it live — Riftwalk in, Nether Blade auto for the mana and burst, then E. I am buying time, not taking over.

edits.before: This is where most of my matchups flip in my favor — but Lillia is a fellow AP scaler, so she contests it. Her R sleep into stacked passive DOT plus Liandry's still punishes my Riftwalk, and her E/W movespeed means I can blink in but rarely pin her down. Void Stone's 15% magic reduction and my Q shield blank some of her burst, which is the one thing keeping me healthy enough to fight, but I cannot stomp the 2+ item window the way I would versus a melee bruiser. Engage her only when her R is down, and lean on the team to lock her so my burst lands.
edits.after: This is where most of my matchups flip in my favor — but Lillia is a fellow AP scaler, so she contests it. Lilting Lullaby into stacked Dream Dust plus Liandry's still punishes my Riftwalk, and her Blooming Blows movespeed means I can blink in but rarely pin her down. Void Stone's 10% magic reduction and my Q shield blank her magic, but neither touches the true damage on the rim of Blooming Blows — so stand inside the ring, never on its edge. Engage clean of Dream Dust and lean on the team to lock her.

notes: Two data-file problems worth fixing at the generator, not per matchup. (1) champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json carries 'Lillia can cancel your Null Sphere (Q) with Lilting Lullaby (R) — only channel once their CC is spent.' That is inverted: Null Sphere INTERRUPTS channels, it is not itself a channel. The rule appears to match on the word 'channels' in Riot's Null Sphere text, and the same bad entry is attached to nine of the fourteen matchups in this slice. I did not write it into any string. (2) The same file says 'Lillia can deny your mobility (Riftwalk (R)) with Swirlseed (E)' off a 'terrain' flag on Swirlseed. Riot's text only says the seed rolls until it hits a wall — it does not create terrain, and nothing in it grounds. Not written either. CHAMPION-WIDE, VERIFIED ON THE WIKI, AFFECTS EVERY KASSADIN PAGE: (a) Void Stone is 10% magic damage reduction, not 15% — reduced in V11.24. The '15%' string appears in roughly a dozen matchups across this champion; '15%' and '10%' are the same length so the fix applies cleanly everywhere. (b) Force Pulse has not been charge-gated since V12.23; it is a 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown that ability casts within 1800 units reduce by 1 second each. The boilerplate 'E only charges when spells fly' in phases[2].why is present on every single matchup page for this champion and is wrong on all of them. Also unedited: full.diff is HARD while diffRating is 5.5/10; I aligned the prose to HARD rather than move a rating off a 15-game sample.
